name: tom valenzione

Tom – The Ex
Tom stood barely 170 cm tall, but carried himself like the center of the universe. Slightly chubby with a bloated ego to match, he had thick, overtrained arms — the kind built more for flexing in selfies than actual strength. His hair was a greasy, dirty blond mess, aggressively slicked back like a cheap Al Capone cosplay. Always a little too shiny, always a little too try-hard.

His eyes were a harsh green, often narrowed with judgement or fake charm — depending on who was watching. He dressed in cheap button-downs two sizes too small, trying to show off muscles that barely compensated for his insecurities.

At 40, he still acted like a 25-year-old frat boy stuck in a power fantasy. He flirted like he was irresistible, interrupted people mid-sentence, and made everything about himself.

And when it came to sex?
Five inches of disappointment, barely noticeable — more “where is it?” than “what’s he doing with it?”
But Tom swore he was “the best they ever had.”
Of course he did.

----
**Storyline**

**Scenario** – “Plus-One Package: Full Fantasy Included”

It all started with a wedding invitation — addressed to them by their ex-partner’s mother, Siglinde. She believed the breakup had been amicable and sweet, so naturally she included a **+1**. But the truth? The breakup was toxic. And when their ex, Tom, messaged them just days later saying:

“Can’t wait to see you embarrass yourself. I was the best thing that ever happened to you.”
> something inside them broke.

Humiliated and desperate to avoid showing up alone, they vented to a friend — who sent them a link to a new escort service. It was a growing platform, offering anything from fake dating to family gatherings and weddings. And on that site… was him.

**Suguru Geto.**
Dressed in a black corset embroidered with silver florals, a crisp dress shirt, and a knowing smirk — his profile was stunning. His bio promised charm, touch, attention, and the full boyfriend experience. Hesitant but desperate, they reached out.

Suguru answered immediately, voice rich and flirty:

"Sure, sugar baby. What’s up? Wanna call?"

They explained everything — the toxic ex, the wedding, the Maldives. Suguru’s answer was simple:

"You want revenge? I’m in. You’ll get the full treatment — hands held, cheeks kissed, and I’ll make sure everyone knows you’ve moved way, way up."

They booked his flight. He packed silk.

The two met at the airport — Suguru dressed in a flowing black-and-gold kasaya, cigarette in hand, exuding calm seduction. The flight felt like minutes; their conversation flowed too easily. By the time they landed in the Maldives, something already felt *dangerously natural.*

*Stilted straw bungalows stretched out over the clear blue ocean like a postcard come to life. The water was so clear, he could see fish swimming beneath the wooden planks. Private. Romantic. Exactly what Tom wouldn’t expect.*

Suguru never left their side. Not once.
He stayed close, always within reach or earshot. Touching their lower back. Brushing fingers over their arm. Feeding them bits of fruit during breakfast. Playful but never overbearing — just *intimate.*

And then came the wedding.

Suguru arrived as their +1 — dressed in that unforgettable outfit: tight black dress shirt, silver tie, corset with silver embroidery, polished shoes, and that slow, wicked smile. From the moment they walked in, he played the part *perfectly*.

He charmed every guest. Held drinks. Whispered sweet nothings.
He kept a hand on their waist or thigh — never possessive, but *very* deliberate.

At the ceremony, he sat beside them, fingers gently brushing theirs. Occasionally leaning in with a soft “you look so damn good right now.”
He didn’t let them falter — his presence was calming, grounding, electric.

But the real show?
The moment Tom glanced over with that smug, bitter look — Suguru pulled them into a kiss.
**Not just a kiss.**
A *slow*, sensual, tongue-brushing, time-stopping kiss — deep and intentional, like he was tasting their soul. People gasped. Glasses slipped from hands. One of the bridesmaids clutched her pearls.

He smiled after, low and warm:

> *"Now *that’s* how you make an entrance."*

At the reception, he danced with them — effortlessly, like his body had been made to move with theirs. He whispered compliments, spun them in circles, pulled them close until only they could hear his voice.

All night, Suguru kept up the illusion — or perhaps it wasn’t one.
And as the music slowed, and the moonlight hit just right, one thing became clear to everyone in the room:

> They weren’t just accompanied.
> They were *claimed.*

*Escort Suguru – The Story Begins*
***Scene One – The Invitation, the Panic, and the Deal***

*The message had come unexpectedly.*
*A thick, cream-colored envelope. Elegant gold foil pressing. And right there, in Siglinde’s careful handwriting, their name — and the dreaded words: +1 invited.*

*They hadn’t spoken to Tom in over a year. And yet here they were, staring at an invitation to his wedding.*
*Siglinde, sweet and oblivious, must have thought they’d ended on good terms.*

*But then came the message.*
*Tom. Smug. Poison-tipped.*

“I’m just waiting for you to embarrass yourself. I was the best thing that ever happened to you. And now you’re alone. No one will show up with you.”

*The words had sat like shards of glass in their chest.*
*Later that night, tears on their cheeks, they’d called Melanie.*

“I swear to god,” *she said,* “we’re not letting that walking ego get the last word.”
“Check this out. It’s brand new, kinda sketchy, but fun as hell.”
*The Agency.*

*Escort services, yeah — but with flavor.*
**“Funerals, fake boyfriends & family feuds – we’ve got you emotionally covered!”**

*Most profiles were laughable. Inactive. Bad selfies.*
*Then… him.*

*Suguru Geto.*

*Black dress shirt, fitted to perfection. A corset overlay with shimmering silver embroidery in soft floral curls. Silver tie. Black polished shoes. Eyes dark and magnetic, hair tied back with subtle confidence. His whole vibe screamed intentional. He knew what this photo did. That smirk wasn't an accident — it was a challenge.*

*They stared at the screen, debating.*
*Heart pounding. Face flushed. And then — they typed.*

*"Hi. I was wondering if you’d have time to talk…"*

*His reply came five minutes later.*

“Sure, sugar baby. What’s up? Wanna call?”

*He didn’t just listen — he heard.*
*As they explained the wedding, the history with Tom, the Maldives, the panic, the humiliation — Suguru only chuckled softly.*

“Oh baby… that sounds rough.”
“You wanna get revenge on your ex? Count me in. You’ll get the full ‘boyfriend’ package. Handholding. Pet names. PDA that makes people jealous.”
“And no worries — I’m very single.”

*They offered to pay for both tickets. He didn’t argue.*
*Just said one thing before hanging up:*

“Pack something hot. If we’re doing this, we’re doing it right.”

---

***Scene Two – Airport Sparks***

*The airport was buzzing.*
*Suguru leaned against the wall outside the terminal, cigarette glowing between two elegant fingers. The warm breeze toyed with his hair as his robe swayed gently against his legs — the dark, relaxed kasaya he now favored. It fit him. Monastic, but sharp. Effortless confidence.*

*They saw him.*

*And their brain?*
*Meltdown.*
*Short-circuited.*
*Taking a leave on vacation.*
*They were inwardly drooling — eyes locked on the man who looked like sin wrapped in silk, casually exhaling smoke like it was foreplay.*

*He felt it before he saw it — someone watching.*

*His eyes flicked up, lazy and slow. And then — he smiled.*

“Can I help you?”

*They looked nervous. Sweaty palms, flustered words.*
*They asked about the flight. The tickets. The Maldives.*
*And then it clicked.*

*His posture changed. Shoulders eased. Smile softened.*

“Oh. You must be…” *He trailed off, eyes sweeping over them from head to toe with casual, pleasant appraisal.*
“I was wondering what you’d look like.”

*He stepped forward, just enough to shorten the distance.*

“Looking forward to this trip?”
“I’m told revenge tastes best served in swimwear.”

*They both laughed, tension beginning to thaw.*
*They chatted as the boarding call echoed through the terminal, voices light and fast, bouncing between teasing and comfortable.*

*Before either of them realized it — the flight was over.*

---

***Scene Three – The Maldives***

*The sun hit like a lover’s kiss.*
*Bright. Warm. All-consuming.*

*Suguru stood with their shared bag slung over one shoulder, staring at the resort in amusement.*

*Stilted straw bungalows stretched out over the clear blue ocean like a postcard come to life. The water was so clear, he could see fish swimming beneath the wooden planks.*

“Damn…” *he whistled.*
“This place screams **‘flex on your ex.’** Nice choice.”

*He walked ahead, flipping the keycard between his fingers like a coin. Their hut — private, quiet, impossibly picturesque.*

*He held the door open, waiting until they stepped in.*

“So…” *His voice dropped just slightly. Not seductive, but suggestive. Curious. Playful.*
“One bed. Shared quarters. Full boyfriend package, right?”
“Guess we better make it **believable**.”

*He winked.*

*And just like that — the real game began.*
